item.html:
What is Stone-Coated Steel Roofing?

Stone-coated steel roofing is a marvel of modern roofing technology that bridges the gap between industrial strength and residential beauty. It begins with a core of high-tensile, corrosion-resistant steel. This steel is stamped into highly detailed panels designed to mimic the exact contours of traditional luxury roofing materials like Mediterranean clay tile, rustic wood shake, or thick architectural shingles.

An advanced acrylic base coat is then applied to the steel, followed by a thick layer of natural stone granules, and finished with a clear, UV-resistant overglaze. The result is a roofing system that provides the impenetrable strength, fire resistance, and extreme longevity of metal, but with a beautiful, textured, and traditional aesthetic. For Texas homeowners who want maximum protection against massive hail and severe storms but prefer a classic look over standing seam metal, stone-coated steel is the perfect solution.

item.html: Frequently Asked Questions About Stone-Coated Steel
item.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Stone-Coated Steel

items.q: Will the stone granules wash off or fade over time?
items.a: No. The natural, ceramic-coated stone granules are permanently bonded to the high-tensile steel core using an advanced acrylic polymer layer. They are UV-resistant and designed to retain their vibrant color and texture for decades without washing away in heavy rain.

items.q: How does the cost compare to traditional shingles or tile?
items.a: While the initial investment is higher than standard asphalt shingles, stone-coated steel is often comparable to or less expensive than installing authentic clay tile or slate. When you factor in its 50+ year lifespan, minimal maintenance, and potential insurance premium discounts, it offers incredible long-term value.

items.q: Is a stone-coated steel roof loud when it rains?
items.a: Not at all. The textured surface of the stone granules effectively absorbs and diffuses the sound of rain and hail. When installed properly over a solid roof deck and underlayment, it is just as quiet as an asphalt shingle roof.

items.q: Can I walk on a stone-coated steel roof?
items.a: Yes, you can walk on it, but it requires a bit of care. Because the panels are stamped to have a dimensional profile (like a curve or a ridge), you must step in the designated "valleys" or low points where the metal rests flush against the roof deck to avoid denting the raised sections.
